Primary: CNBC quote endpoint, read 08:15:26 BST. Cross-check: Trading Economics (UK 10Y, US 10Y, GB100, Brent).

*** THE FTSE FEED IS LIVE AT 08:15 TODAY ***
.FTSE returned 10,805.95, -0.32%, stamped 2026-10-16T08:00 — a genuine intraday price barely half an
hour after the open, not yesterday's close carried forward. That is earlier than the feed has
cooperated on any day this week (the lag has usually run to about 08:45). Two confirmations that this
is real: the stamp carries today's date, and CNBC's previous_day_closing of 10,840.35 matches our own
published evening figure to the decimal. Trading Economics GB100 gives 10,814.48 -0.24% on a slightly
later read — about 9 points higher and the same direction, which is ordinary provider drift on a
moving index rather than a disagreement.
NOTE: the scheduled run that was killed at 08:13 had fetched the quote endpoint at about 08:04 and got
the FTSE still stamped 2026-10-15. So the feed went live between 08:04 and 08:15 this morning.

*** FOUR INSTRUMENTS WHERE LAST NIGHT'S PUBLISHED FIGURE WAS AN INTRADAY READ, NOT A CLOSE ***
Last night's edition was published at 18:13 and read live at 18:13, with Wall Street open until 21:00.
The settled closes, now visible as CNBC's previous_day_closing, came in differently — and in every
case the move continued in the same direction after we read it:
  S&P 500  published 7,727.08 +0.11 intraday -> actual close 7,744.06 +0.33
  Brent    published  106.15  +0.08 intraday -> actual settle  105.92
  Gold     published 4,147.44 +1.03 intraday -> actual close  4,170.245
  VIX      published   16.82  -0.30 intraday -> actual close    16.46
  UST      published    5.09  -0.10 intraday -> actual close     5.087
None of these is an error in last night's edition — an intraday read and a close are different things
and the ticker said so. But this morning's change figures are computed against the CLOSES, which is
the only consistent basis. The S&P carries Thursday's close with Thursday's move, declared, because
Wall Street does not open until 14:30 BST.

*** GILT: ALL THREE SOURCES AGREE ON THE LEVEL AND THE DIRECTION FOR ONCE ***
  CNBC:              5.3604, change -0.0157 (prev 5.3761)  -> -0.02
  Trading Economics: 5.36,   day change -0.004              -> -0.00
  Our own series:    5.37 published last night -> 5.36 now  -> -0.01
PUBLISHED: 5.36, -0.01 — our own series, which sits between the two providers, as all week.
The spread is 1.5bp, the narrowest this week, and the three agree the gilt is a shade lower and still
above 5.3%. Worth recording that CNBC's previous-close field, which was incoherent yesterday evening
(it had drifted to 5.3761, within a basis point of the then-live level), is now coherent: 5.3761 is a
plausible Thursday close and is consistent with Trading Economics' 5.37.

*** UST ***
CNBC 5.077, -0.01 against a 5.087 close. Trading Economics 5.08, +0.003. Both effectively flat and
agreeing on the level. PUBLISHED 5.08, -0.01.

*** BRENT: TRADING ECONOMICS IS NOT USABLE AS CORROBORATION THIS MORNING ***
CNBC @LCO.1 105.27 -0.61% stamped 08:05, against a 105.92 settle — coherent.
Trading Economics' Brent page returned 97.26 -0.72%, which is roughly eight dollars below CNBC and
below where its own readings have sat all week; yesterday the same scrape pattern returned a WTI-like
94.13 from a page labelled Brent. The most likely explanation is that the scrape is picking up the
wrong row rather than that one provider is eight dollars wrong. It is NOT treated as a second source
for Brent today, and the direction (down) is the only thing taken from it.

*** OVERNIGHT: RISK APPETITE KEPT RECOVERING ***
The VIX closed at 16.46 and is now 16.03, down a further 2.61% — two consecutive falls, having spiked
3.7% at this time yesterday. Gold is up 0.34% to 4,184.48, a fresh high for the week. Sterling is
firmer again at 1.3315, up 0.32%, its best level this week. The FTSE is the exception, opening 0.32%
lower after yesterday's 1.08% close, which is a pause rather than a reversal.

yesterday's 5.3761 close, and the published figure was going to be 5.36 / -0.01. At 08:33 it reads

PUBLISHED: 5.37, 0.00. A zero is unusual and is stated as read rather than nudged to -0.01 to look
